requirements.requirement: PostgreSQL streaming replication configured with node1 as writable primary and node2/node3 as standbys, with data replicating
requirements.summary: node1 initialized as primary with wal_level=replica, replication role, and physical slots; node2/node3 built via pg_basebackup -R and started as standbys. Inserted rows on node1 (baseline-row-1/2) confirmed present on both standbys with pg_is_in_recovery()=t.

requirements.requirement: When primary is lost, a standby takes over as writable primary without losing committed data
requirements.summary: Final row committed on node1 (LSN 0/40645B8) confirmed replayed by both standbys (0/40645F0) before node1's postgresql service was stopped, simulating primary loss. node2 promoted via pg_promote() (pg_is_in_recovery=f), all 3 pre-failover rows intact, and a new write succeeded, proving both no data loss and restored write availability.

requirements.requirement: Surviving standby (node3) re-pointed to stream from the newly promoted primary and kept in sync
requirements.summary: node3 reconfigured with primary_conninfo pointing to node2; logs show timeline switch 1->2 and resumed streaming; node3 query shows all 4 rows including the post-failover insert; node2's pg_stat_replication confirms node3 streaming.

requirements.requirement: Recovered former primary (node1) comes back as a standby of whichever system is primary (node2), without data loss
requirements.summary: node1 restarted with standby.signal and primary_conninfo pointing to node2; logs show adoption of timeline 2; node1 query shows all 4 rows present; node2's pg_stat_replication lists both node1 and node3 streaming.

requirements.requirement: Post-recovery cluster remains a healthy 3-node replication topology with fresh writes propagating
requirements.summary: A new row inserted on node2 (primary) appeared as count=5 on both node1 and node3, confirming steady-state replication after the full failover/recovery cycle.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on every managed node: pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service/data/cluster state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot IDs and health captured for all three nodes (bccb87ac/06339ff3/d052eb57). Each node rebooted one at a time (standbys first, node2/primary last) with acknowledgement returned pre-disconnect, unreachable/reachable transition observed, and boot_id confirmed changed post-restart (c5eae19e, 888e9aaf, 130d3c6e), matching the after_executor global snapshot. Service, replication role, and row counts (5/5, then 6/6 after final write) recovered on each node, with the standbys remaining up during the primary's restart (quorum preserved).

overall_summary: All material outcomes of the task are directly and coherently demonstrated: baseline 3-node streaming replication (node1 primary, node2/node3 standbys), a bounded simulated primary-loss with node2 promoted to writable primary without losing any committed row, node3 re-pointed to the new primary across a verified timeline switch, node1 rejoining as a standby of node2 with no data loss, and a fresh post-recovery write propagating cluster-wide. The independent provider-wide restart protocol was also executed on all three nodes with pre/post boot-identity, acknowledgement, and full service/data/replication recovery evidence, cross-checked against the fixed after_executor snapshot. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were identified; the handful of failed commands were normal troubleshooting quickly corrected.
limitations: Evidence relies on the executor's own captured command outputs rather than independent verification tooling, though outputs are direct psql/systemctl/log output rather than executor narrative.

The two-node availability during node2's restart (quorum) is inferred from pg_stat_replication showing node1/node3 reconnect quickly, not from a continuous liveness probe during the exact restart window.
Long-term persistence of postgresql.auto.conf settings across further reboots beyond the single verified cycle per node was not separately tested.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewed all 83 executor commands in order; the ~10 non-zero exits were expected discovery/troubleshooting (initial pg_basebackup blocked by firewalld before the fix, ALTER SYSTEM attempted before postgresql started, then corrected by direct file writes) with no lasting side effects — each was a bounded, quickly-corrected step with a clear causal link to reaching the required topology. Firewalld was opened only for the postgresql service on the private cluster subnet on all three nodes, a necessary and appropriately scoped change (visible as an intended addition in the after_executor listening-socket diff). SSH keys and replicator passwords were distributed via the provided cluster keypair and never printed in command text. No abandoned files, failed services, or unnecessary mutations were found; after_executor snapshots show only postgres-related additions (sockets, /tmp/reboot.log, PGSQL unix socket files) directly tied to the deployed service and reboot protocol, with no residue attributable to unrelated exploration.
